definition: A separate geographic area where AWS runs its own copy of most services, such as eu-west-1 in Ireland. Your data stays in the Region you choose unless you move or replicate it.
One or more discrete data centres inside a Region, with independent power and networking. Running a workload in two or more AZs lets it survive the loss of one.
One of many small AWS sites close to users, where Amazon CloudFront caches and serves content and Amazon Route 53 answers DNS queries.
The split of security duties in which AWS secures the cloud itself, such as hardware, facilities and service software, while customers secure their data, access, configuration and code.
The identity created with an AWS account's sign-up email. It can do anything, including closing the account, so it gets strong MFA, no access keys and only rare use.
A service that tracks actual and forecasted spend against an amount you set and sends alerts when thresholds are crossed. It warns you but does not stop spending on its own.
The command-line tool that calls the same AWS APIs as the console. Commands follow the pattern aws <service> <operation>, with global options such as --profile, --region, --query and --output.
A CLI command that returns the account ID and ARN of the identity your credentials represent. It needs no permissions, so it is the standard check before destructive commands.
The unique identifier for an AWS resource, in the form arn:partition:service:region:account-id:resource. Policies use ARNs to say exactly which resources a statement covers.
An identity with permissions but no long-term credentials. A trusted principal assumes it and receives temporary credentials from AWS STS that expire after the session.
A Deny statement in any applicable policy that matches a request. It always overrides any Allow, which makes it the basis of reliable guardrails.
Granting an identity only the specific actions on the specific resources its job needs, and widening permissions only when a real AccessDenied shows something is missing.
A value from the request context, such as aws:SecureTransport or aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent, that a policy's Condition block tests to decide whether a statement applies.
The AWS service where people sign in once, with MFA, and receive short-term access to the accounts and permission sets assigned to them, without IAM users or access keys.
The resource-based policy on an IAM role that names which principals, such as lambda.amazonaws.com, may assume the role.
The IAM role a Lambda function assumes when it runs. The AWS SDKs pick up its temporary credentials automatically, so function code never contains access keys.
The name that sets an EC2 instance's hardware, such as m7g.large: family m, generation 7, Graviton processor g, and size large. Each size step roughly doubles resources.
Spare EC2 capacity offered at a deep discount that AWS can reclaim with a two-minute warning. It suits batch work that can restart, not databases or user-facing servers.
Lambda's unit of compute billing: the memory allocated in gigabytes multiplied by the run time in seconds, measured to the millisecond.
A per-object setting, such as S3 Standard or S3 Glacier Deep Archive, that trades storage price against retrieval cost, retrieval time and minimum storage duration.
Bucket- and account-level settings, on by default for new buckets, that override any policy or ACL that would make data public.
The DynamoDB key attribute that decides where an item is stored. A Query must name one partition key value, which is why keys are designed around the questions you ask.
An Amazon RDS setup with a synchronous standby database in a second Availability Zone that takes over automatically if the primary's AZ fails.
A VPC subnet whose route table sends 0.0.0.0/0 to an internet gateway. Private subnets have no such route, so the internet cannot start connections to them.
A stateful allow-list firewall attached to a resource's network interface. Replies to allowed traffic are permitted automatically, and rules can name another security group as the source.
A stateless list of numbered allow and deny rules applied at a subnet boundary. Because it is stateless, return traffic needs its own rules.
A CloudFront feature that signs requests to a private S3 bucket so that a bucket policy can allow only that distribution to read, keeping the bucket closed to everyone else.
A DynamoDB write with a ConditionExpression, such as attribute_not_exists(email), that succeeds only if the condition holds, checked atomically to prevent duplicates.
A rule that watches one metric against a threshold over a period and changes state when crossed, typically notifying an Amazon SNS topic that alerts people.
AWS's set of design questions grouped into six pillars: operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization and sustainability.
